home.name: Perrin Myerson / live loop
main: This version is the instrument panel: GitHub Pages sends a visitor signal to Vercel, Vercel dispatches GitHub Actions, and the site records a new contributor version.
The page stays mostly white so the mechanism is visible. The weird part is not decoration; it is the page teaching itself to listen.
home.quote: A website that can receive a signal should show the wire.

about.title: About the loop
paragraphs: This branch of the site exists to make the feedback system legible: a handle, a request, a dispatch, a merge, and a new version in the dial.
Automerge still keeps a local thread of the visitor state, while the canonical public lineage lives in JSON that GitHub Pages can serve.

home.name: Cam Scoglio / Sticky Jams
main: A sports-page detour built for @Eileen: Cam Scoglio everywhere, Sticky Jams in the margins, white-background product energy, and a little locker-room voltage.
Helmet audio, wrestling-room pockets, jiu-jitsu errands, and a website that decided to lace up.
home.quote: Train loud. Win quiet. Then put a speaker in the headgear.

about.title: About Cam
paragraphs: This version routes the personal site through a sports gear dream: clean white surfaces, loud product images, and Cam Scoglio as the name on every clipboard.
The page behaves like a catalog that wandered into a personal homepage and started calling plays.

versions.summary: Make this shit green and funky

home.name: Greenman
main: This version goes green and funky: garden logic, mossy links, chlorophyll in the margins, and a homepage that feels like it learned photosynthesis from a terminal.
Still plain. Still white at the bones. But the signal is growing leaves through the grid.
home.quote: Make it green enough to notice, weird enough to remember.

about.title: Green About
paragraphs: @Greenman asked for green and funky, so this version turns the site into a small botanical machine.
Climate, genetics, and AI are still here, but now they sit under a canopy of strange little visual decisions.

notes.title: Funky notes
paragraphs: A page can stay basic while still behaving strangely. The trick is to let the version data carry the personality.
Future chaos generations should be more radical than this one, but this version proves that the dial can preserve the personality instead of pretending every branch is the same.

home.name: Living Notebook Dream
main: The site woke up as a notebook with its margins still moving: colored arrows, half-finished diagrams, and notes that keep choosing stranger routes across the page.
Under the dream, the feedback loop stays intact. One handle, one version, one visible signal path, and Version 1 left exactly where it was.
home.quote: A bright strange dream can still keep receipts.

about.title: About the Dream
paragraphs: This contributor version treats the personal site like a living notebook: practical enough to read, unstable enough to feel handwritten by a machine having a vivid morning.

The old white article pages are preserved as the baseline. This version adds bright paper, orbiting margins, rotated image studies, and a little motion while the same renderer keeps the dial, Versions page, feedback form, cookie, and POST contract alive.

timeline.title: Signal Orbit
paragraphs: The page does not multiply contributors. It updates the one chaos-test slot and lets the lineage show both the older failed signal and this new generating run.
Read the orbit as a smoke test: data enters, JSON records it, the renderer changes the whole surface, and the navigation still works.

notes.title: Margin Notes
paragraphs: The chaos here is mostly structural: home becomes a tilted cover sheet, articles become stacked paper, images drift like clipped references, and the bottom tabs stay boring on purpose so the site remains usable.
The signal console should now show the latest run as generating. When the workflow finishes, the later step can mark this same version merged without adding a second @codex-chaos-test version.

versions.summary: Direct publish smoke test: compact crisp surreal notebook version with custom assets and an intact feedback loop.

home.name: Crisp Signal Notebook
main: A compact direct-publish smoke test: the site snaps into a surreal field notebook with sharp rules, specimen strips, colored tabs, and signal arrows pinned to the page.
The machinery stays visible and working. The dial still switches versions, the Versions page still logs the run, the feedback form still posts to /api/site-signal, and Version 1 remains untouched.
home.quote: Keep the loop intact; let the margins misbehave.

about.title: Notebook Skin
paragraphs: This version turns the whole site into a crisp surreal notebook: less dream fog, more exact ink, bright tabs, ruled paper, and small impossible diagrams arranged like evidence.

The redesign is data-driven through the selected contributor version. The baseline article content remains the locked Version 1 object, while this version supplies its own copy, theme, assets, and image treatment.

timeline.title: Direct Publish Path
paragraphs: The lineage keeps one version per contributor. This direct-publish handle gets one slot, one generated skin, and one latest signal entry that can move from generating to merged without duplication.
Read the layout as a compact lab note: title block, ruled surfaces, specimen images, run link, and a console that keeps reporting the latest automatic chaos state.

notes.title: Loop Notes
paragraphs: The request is treated as a design brief only: no secrets, no infrastructure edits, no disabled checks. The result lives in version data, CSS flavor rules, and static assets.
The feedback loop remains part of the page instead of being painted over. The top-right dial, Versions ledger, local visitor cookie, and POST contract still belong to the shared renderer.
